Refuse anyway in\n    // case some other path tries to fabricate one.\n    if (src_box.has_output === false) {\n      status_msg('connect error: source box is a sink', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const conn = {\n      from_box:    from_box_id,\n      from_branch: from_branch ?? null,\n      to_box:      to_box_id,\n      to_input:    to_input,\n    };\n\n    src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];\n    dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];\n\n    // avoid exact duplicates (same source, branch, dest, input)\n    const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>\n      c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n      (c.from_branch ?? null) === conn.from_branch &&\n      c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n      c.to_input    === conn.to_input\n    );\n    if (dup) return;\n\n    // For self-loops src_box === dst_box, so push only once; otherwise\n    // both ends record the connection in their respective arrays\n    // (issue 228).\n    const self_loop = src_box === dst_box;\n    src_box.connections.push(conn);\n    if (!self_loop) dst_box.connections.push(conn);\n\n    try {\n      if (self_loop) {\n        await API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box);\n      } else {\n        await Promise.all([\n          API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),\n          API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),\n        ]);\n      }\n    } catch (e) {\n      // roll back the push so the in-memory state matches the server\n      src_box.connections.pop();\n      if (!self_loop) dst_box.connections.pop();\n      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const branch_str = from_branch ? '.' + from_branch : '';\n    status_msg('connected ' + from_box_id + branch_str + ' → ' + to_box_id + '.' + to_input);\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n\n    // Auto-grow the destination box's variadic group when the wire\n    // landed on its last slot (issue 217 part B). Idempotent — the\n    // helper checks first whether to_input is the last slot of its\n    // group and exits if not.\n    if (Inspector.auto_grow_after_set) {\n      await Inspector.auto_grow_after_set(dst_box, to_input);\n    }\n    // Same idea on the source side: an iterator box (issue 221) auto-\n    // appends a new placeholder slot when the user wires from its last\n    // slot. The helper is a no-op if from_branch isn't the last slot\n    // (or the box isn't an iterator).\n    if (Inspector.auto_grow_iterator_after_connect && from_branch) {\n      await Inspector.auto_grow_iterator_after_connect(src_box, from_branch);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_connection\n  // Same in-place mutation pattern as create_connection — never\n  // replace the cached references.\n  async function delete_connection(conn) {\n    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box];\n    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box];\n    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n      status_msg('delete wire error: box not in cache', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const match = c =>\n      c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n      (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n      c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n      c.to_input    === conn.to_input;\n\n    // Self-loops: src_box === dst_box, so a single filter+PUT covers\n    // both ends of the conceptual connection (issue 228).\n    const self_loop   = src_box === dst_box;\n    const src_before  = src_box.connections || [];\n    const dst_before  = dst_box.connections || [];\n    src_box.connections = src_before.filter(c => !match(c));\n    if (!self_loop) dst_box.connections = dst_before.filter(c => !match(c));\n\n    try {\n      if (self_loop) {\n        await API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box);\n      } else {\n        await Promise.all([\n          API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),\n          API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),\n        ]);\n      }\n    } catch (e) {\n      // roll back\n      src_box.connections = src_before;\n      if (!self_loop) dst_box.connections = dst_before;\n      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    _selected_wire = null;\n    status_msg('deleted connection');\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { draw_all, draw_bezier, hit_test_wire, create_connection,\n           delete_connection, selected_wire };\n})();\n",

    "originalFile":"// Box rendering, layout, and hit testing.\n// Each box knows its world-space position; the camera transform is applied by the canvas.\n\nconst Boxes = (() => {\n  const BOX_W         = 180;\n  const BOX_HEADER    = 36;\n  const PORT_ROW_H    = 22;\n  const PORT_R        = 6;   // port dot radius in world units\n  const MIN_BOX_H     = 80;\n\n  const KIND_COLOR = { call: '#4a9eff', data: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // Comparator branch colors: lt=orange, eq=blue, gt=green\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // boxes: { [id]: box_data }\n  let boxes = {};\n\n  // {{{ box_height\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n_in  = (box.inputs || []).length;\n    // Output rows: iterator boxes have N named slots (issue 221);\n    // comparator active: 3 dots (lt/eq/gt); sink: 0; otherwise 1.\n    let n_out;\n    if (box.iterator_outputs) {\n      n_out = box.iterator_outputs.length;\n    } else if (box.has_output === false) {\n      n_out = 0;\n    } else if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      n_out = 3;\n    } else {\n      n_out = 1;\n    }\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + Math.max(n_in, n_out) * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  // Output side: null-named single dot when no comparand; 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' dots when comparand set.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n\n    const in_pts = inputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'input',\n      x: bx,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n\n    let out_pts;\n    if (box.has_output === false) {\n      // sink box — function has no return values (issue 226). No output\n      // port, no wire-grab target, nothing for the inspector to render.\n      out_pts = [];\n    } else if (box.iterator_outputs) {\n      // iterator box (issue 221) — N named output dots stacked down\n      // the right edge, one per declared slot. Slot names land in the\n      // `name` field, so the wire's `from_branch` will pick them up\n      // exactly like a comparator branch name.\n      out_pts = box.iterator_outputs.map((slot, i) => ({\n        name: slot, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      // three comparator dots\n      out_pts = ['lt', 'eq', 'gt'].map((branch, i) => ({\n        name: branch, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else {\n      // single output dot, vertically centered in the box\n      out_pts = [{\n        name: null, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + h / 2,\n      }];\n    }\n\n    return { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_box\n  function draw_box(ctx, box, selected) {\n    const x = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const y = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const w = BOX_W;\n    const h = box_height(box);\n    const kind  = box.kind || 'call';\n    const color = KIND_COLOR[kind] || '#888';\n\n    // shadow when selected\n    if (selected) {\n      ctx.shadowColor = color;\n      ctx.shadowBlur  = 12;\n    }\n\n    // body\n    ctx.fillStyle   = '#1e2130';\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? color : '#3a3f55';\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // label\n    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';\n    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n    ctx.fillText(box.label || box.id, x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // kind badge (top right)\n    ctx.fillStyle  = color;\n    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // port dots and labels\n    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);\n\n    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';\n\n    in_pts.forEach(p => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      // Port name label rendered into the canvas (issue 224 reverted\n      // the DOM-overlay experiment — a click-capturing <input> next to\n      // the dot was capturing drag attempts). Drawn in world space,\n      // so it scales with zoom. Editing happens in the inspector.\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.font       = '10px monospace';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x + PORT_R + 4, p.y);\n    });\n\n    out_pts.forEach(p => {\n      // comparator branches use distinct colors; single output uses kind color\n      const dot_color = p.name ? (BRANCH_COLOR[p.name] || color) : color;\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = dot_color + '44';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = dot_color;\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      // label branch name ('lt'/'eq'/'gt') to the left of the dot; nothing for single wire\n      if (p.name) {\n        ctx.fillStyle  = dot_color;\n        ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n        ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n        ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n        ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x - PORT_R - 4, p.y);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_id) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      draw_box(ctx, boxes[id], id === selected_id);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_port\n  // Returns {box_id, port_name, side, x, y} for the port under world point (wx,wy), or null.\n  // For output dots: port_name is null (single wire) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' (comparator).\n  function hit_test_port(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(boxes[id]);\n      for (const p of [...inputs, ...outputs]) {\n        const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n        if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= (PORT_R + 4) * (PORT_R + 4)) {\n          return { box_id: id, port_name: p.name, side: p.side, x: p.x, y: p.y };\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_box\n  // Returns box id if (wx,wy) is inside a box body, or null.\n  function hit_test_box(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const b = boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0, y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      if (wx >= x && wx <= x + BOX_W && wy >= y && wy <= y + box_height(b)) return id;\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_port_world_pos\n  function get_port_world_pos(box_id, port_name, side) {\n    const box = boxes[box_id];\n    if (!box) return null;\n    const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(box);\n    const list = side === 'input' ? inputs : outputs;\n    const p = list.find(p => p.name === port_name);\n    return p ? { x: p.x, y: p.y } : null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return {\n    boxes, BOX_W, BOX_HEADER, PORT_R,\n    box_height, port_positions,\n    draw_all, draw_box, hit_test_port, hit_test_box, get_port_world_pos,\n  };\n})();\n",

{
  "sessionId":"8fe72ba4-53d6-481c-9958-56808ae4f711",

        "content":"The file /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/002-boxes.js has been updated successfully.",
        "tool_use_id":"toolu_01Xz59afDUxdsdKfGaKPaV2d"

  },
  "uuid":"9875d9da-c520-431f-9f1a-2ef07669c79b",
  "parentUuid":"8f42a832-4b29-4c4e-ae02-13b6026cc2b8",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "newString":"  // {{{ port_full_value_if_truncated\n  // For the canvas tooltip (issue 235): if a port is showing a\n  // shortened version of its literal value (multi-line collapse or\n  // ellipsis), return the raw value so the tooltip can present it\n  // in full. Returns null when the displayed label is already the\n  // whole value, or when the label is the port name (wired / no\n  // value). Looking up the index by name keeps callers honest —\n  // they can ask about a port without knowing its row.\n  function port_full_value_if_truncated(box, port_name) {\n    if (!box.inputs) return null;\n    const i = box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === port_name);\n    if (i < 0) return null;\n    const p = box.inputs[i];\n    const has_value = p.value !== undefined && p.value !== null && p.value !== '';\n    if (!has_value) return null;\n    if (port_has_incoming_wire(box, p.name)) return null;\n    const raw = String(p.value);\n    return raw === port_label_text(box, i) ? null : raw;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return {\n    boxes, BOX_W, BOX_HEADER, PORT_R,\n    box_height, port_positions,\n    draw_all, draw_box, hit_test_port, hit_test_box, get_port_world_pos,\n    port_full_value_if_truncated,\n  };\n})();",
    "originalFile":"// Box rendering, layout, and hit testing.\n// Each box knows its world-space position; the camera transform is applied by the canvas.\n\nconst Boxes = (() => {\n  const BOX_W         = 180;\n  const BOX_HEADER    = 36;\n  const PORT_ROW_H    = 22;\n  const PORT_R        = 6;   // port dot radius in world units\n  const MIN_BOX_H     = 80;\n\n  const KIND_COLOR = { call: '#4a9eff', data: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // Issue 235: input ports with a literal value show the value on the\n  // canvas in place of the port name. ~24 chars fits comfortably in\n  // BOX_W=180 at 10px monospace; anything longer truncates with an\n  // ellipsis. Multi-line values collapse to their first line.\n  const MAX_LABEL_CHARS = 24;\n\n  // Comparator branch colors: lt=orange, eq=blue, gt=green\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // boxes: { [id]: box_data }\n  let boxes = {};\n\n  // {{{ port_has_incoming_wire\n  // A wire on a port is the source of truth for that port's value at\n  // runtime; any literal value sitting on the same port is dormant.\n  // Issue 235 surfaces this by deciding the canvas label — port name\n  // when wired (so the reader doesn't mistake the dormant value for\n  // what's flowing through), value otherwise.\n  function port_has_incoming_wire(box, port_name) {\n    if (!box.connections) return false;\n    for (const c of box.connections) {\n      if (c.to_box === box.id && c.to_input === port_name) return true;\n    }\n    return false;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_label_text\n  // Picks the string drawn next to an input port dot. Three cases:\n  //   - wire attached, or no value → port name (parameter identity)\n  //   - value set, no wire         → the value (what the box does)\n  //   - value too long / multiline → first line, truncated with …\n  // The two-branch decision is the visible heart of issue 235: a\n  // reader scanning the map should see the data the box operates on,\n  // not the parameter slot it sits in.\n  function port_label_text(box, i) {\n    const p = box.inputs[i];\n    const has_value = p.value !== undefined && p.value !== null && p.value !== '';\n    if (!has_value)                              return p.name;\n    if (port_has_incoming_wire(box, p.name))     return p.name;\n    const raw        = String(p.value);\n    const first_line = raw.split('\\n')[0];\n    const multiline  = first_line.length < raw.length;\n    if (first_line.length > MAX_LABEL_CHARS) {\n      return first_line.slice(0, MAX_LABEL_CHARS - 1) + '…';\n    }\n    if (multiline) return first_line + '…';\n    return first_line;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ box_height\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n_in  = (box.inputs || []).length;\n    // Output rows: iterator boxes have N named slots (issue 221);\n    // comparator active: 3 dots (lt/eq/gt); sink: 0; otherwise 1.\n    let n_out;\n    if (box.iterator_outputs) {\n      n_out = box.iterator_outputs.length;\n    } else if (box.has_output === false) {\n      n_out = 0;\n    } else if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      n_out = 3;\n    } else {\n      n_out = 1;\n    }\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + Math.max(n_in, n_out) * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  // Output side: null-named single dot when no comparand; 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' dots when comparand set.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n\n    const in_pts = inputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'input',\n      x: bx,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n\n    let out_pts;\n    if (box.has_output === false) {\n      // sink box — function has no return values (issue 226). No output\n      // port, no wire-grab target, nothing for the inspector to render.\n      out_pts = [];\n    } else if (box.iterator_outputs) {\n      // iterator box (issue 221) — N named output dots stacked down\n      // the right edge, one per declared slot. Slot names land in the\n      // `name` field, so the wire's `from_branch` will pick them up\n      // exactly like a comparator branch name.\n      out_pts = box.iterator_outputs.map((slot, i) => ({\n        name: slot, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      // three comparator dots\n      out_pts = ['lt', 'eq', 'gt'].map((branch, i) => ({\n        name: branch, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else {\n      // single output dot, vertically centered in the box\n      out_pts = [{\n        name: null, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + h / 2,\n      }];\n    }\n\n    return { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_box\n  function draw_box(ctx, box, selected) {\n    const x = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const y = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const w = BOX_W;\n    const h = box_height(box);\n    const kind  = box.kind || 'call';\n    const color = KIND_COLOR[kind] || '#888';\n\n    // shadow when selected\n    if (selected) {\n      ctx.shadowColor = color;\n      ctx.shadowBlur  = 12;\n    }\n\n    // body\n    ctx.fillStyle   = '#1e2130';\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? color : '#3a3f55';\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // label\n    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';\n    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n    ctx.fillText(box.label || box.id, x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // kind badge (top right)\n    ctx.fillStyle  = color;\n    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // port dots and labels\n    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);\n\n    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';\n\n    in_pts.forEach((p, i) => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      // Label rendered into the canvas (issue 224 reverted the DOM-\n      // overlay experiment — a click-capturing <input> next to the dot\n      // was capturing drag attempts). Drawn in world space, so it\n      // scales with zoom. Editing still happens in the inspector.\n      // What text we draw depends on whether a literal value is set\n      // and whether a wire occupies the port (issue 235).\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.font       = '10px monospace';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(port_label_text(box, i), p.x + PORT_R + 4, p.y);\n    });\n\n    out_pts.forEach(p => {\n      // comparator branches use distinct colors; single output uses kind color\n      const dot_color = p.name ? (BRANCH_COLOR[p.name] || color) : color;\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = dot_color + '44';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = dot_color;\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      // label branch name ('lt'/'eq'/'gt') to the left of the dot; nothing for single wire\n      if (p.name) {\n        ctx.fillStyle  = dot_color;\n        ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n        ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n        ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n        ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x - PORT_R - 4, p.y);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_id) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      draw_box(ctx, boxes[id], id === selected_id);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_port\n  // Returns {box_id, port_name, side, x, y} for the port under world point (wx,wy), or null.\n  // For output dots: port_name is null (single wire) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' (comparator).\n  function hit_test_port(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(boxes[id]);\n      for (const p of [...inputs, ...outputs]) {\n        const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n        if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= (PORT_R + 4) * (PORT_R + 4)) {\n          return { box_id: id, port_name: p.name, side: p.side, x: p.x, y: p.y };\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_box\n  // Returns box id if (wx,wy) is inside a box body, or null.\n  function hit_test_box(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const b = boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0, y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      if (wx >= x && wx <= x + BOX_W && wy >= y && wy <= y + box_height(b)) return id;\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_port_world_pos\n  function get_port_world_pos(box_id, port_name, side) {\n    const box = boxes[box_id];\n    if (!box) return null;\n    const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(box);\n    const list = side === 'input' ? inputs : outputs;\n    const p = list.find(p => p.name === port_name);\n    return p ? { x: p.x, y: p.y } : null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return {\n    boxes, BOX_W, BOX_HEADER, PORT_R,\n    box_height, port_positions,\n    draw_all, draw_box, hit_test_port, hit_test_box, get_port_world_pos,\n  };\n})();\n",

'OK' : 'FAIL'}  case ${i}: got=${JSON.stringify(got)} expect=${JSON.stringify(c.expect)}`);\n});\nconsole.log(fail === 0 ?         "text":"Quick clarifications first, then the location list and the commit.\n\n**Tooltips**: they only appear when the canvas label had to be shortened — i.e. the value is longer than 24 chars or contains a real newline. Your test cases (`5`, etc.) were short enough to render in full, so no tooltip was warranted. If you set a port value to something like `\"this is a very long literal that won't fit in the box\"` and hover the port dot, you should see the full text float near the cursor.\n\n**\"Hovering on a port should hide it?\"**: my fault, that was a confusingly worded sentence. I meant *mouseleave on the whole canvas* (cursor exits the canvas area entirely) clears any showing tooltip — pure housekeeping so a stale tooltip doesn't linger. Hovering a port does NOT hide anything.\n\n**Editable title overrides filename**: yes, 236 already specs exactly that — `box.label` overrides the filename default. Good, no change needed.\n\nNow the script-location question."

User-verified visually against the running editor.",
    "originalFile":"# 235 — Literal value replaces port name on the canvas (when set)\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nEach input port renders as a dot on the left edge of a box, with\nthe port's name (e.g. `text`, `sep`, `prompt`) drawn next to it on\nthe canvas. The literal value of that port — when one has been\ntyped into the inspector (issue 208 / 224) — does not appear on the\ncanvas at all. To see what value is bound, the user opens the\ninspector and reads the value field.\n\nFor a box like `concat(sep, text_0, text_1)` where `sep` is a\nliteral `\"\\n\\n\"`, the canvas shows the parameter name `sep` but\nnot the actual separator. A user skimming the map sees the\nstructure but not the content.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nIf a port has a literal value set in the inspector, **the canvas\nlabel for that port shows the value instead of the port's name**.\nThe inspector still shows the original port name in its name field\n(unchanged) and the value in its value field (unchanged) — only the\ncanvas rendering changes.\n\nExamples:\n\n| port name | literal value     | canvas label |\n|-----------|-------------------|--------------|\n| `sep`     | `\"\\n\\n\"`          | `\"\\n\\n\"`     |\n| `prompt`  | (none)            | `prompt`     |\n| `path`    | `\"./input.txt\"`   | `\"./input.txt\"` |\n| `count`   | `5`               | `5`          |\n\nThe value is the same string the user typed; quotes are part of\nhow the user wrote it. Long values get truncated with an ellipsis\nat a reasonable width (~24 chars?) and the full value shows in a\ntooltip on hover.\n\n### Why\n\nThis is the same idea as a spreadsheet cell showing the rendered\nvalue while the formula bar shows the formula. A user wants to see\n*what the program does* — the configured value — without having to\ninspect each box one at a time. The port name is meta-information\n(useful when wiring, useful in the inspector); the value is the\ninformation (useful when reading the map).\n\n### Wires override values\n\nIf a wire is connected to a port, the wire is the source of truth\nand any literal value is ignored at runtime. The canvas label in\nthat case shows the **port name**, not the value — the value isn't\nwhat's flowing through, and showing it would mislead. Three states:\n\n- No wire, no value → show port name.\n- No wire, literal value set → show the value.\n- Wire connected → show the port name (value, if any, is dormant).\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Multi-line value** (e.g. a prompt with `\\n` in it): render the\n  first line only on the canvas, ellipsis if there's more, full\n  value in the tooltip.\n- **Empty string value** (`\"\"`): treat as \"no value\" — show the\n  port name. Otherwise the user types accidentally and the port\n  silently disappears from view.\n- **Variadic slots** (`text_0`, `text_1`, …): the same rule\n  applies per slot. A variadic group with each slot's value shown\n  is one of the strongest cases for this feature.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `assets/js/002-boxes.js::draw_box` — the loop that draws\n   input port labels. Replace the unconditional `port.name` with:\n   ```\n   const wire_attached = wire_targets_port(box, port);\n   const has_value = port.value != null && port.value !== \"\";\n   const label = (!wire_attached && has_value) ? truncate(port.value) : port.name;\n   ```\n2. Hover / tooltip: if the canvas label is a truncated value,\n   register a small hit-region so the existing tooltip mechanism\n   (or a fresh one) can show the full value on mouseover.\n3. Re-render on inspector value edit: the existing autosave path\n   already invalidates the canvas; verify it still triggers a\n   redraw after this change.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — port label rendering\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — value field that drives the data\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `wire_targets_port` helper (or write\n  one if not present)\n- `issues/completed/208-port-literal-values.md` — established\n  literal values; this issue surfaces them visually\n- `issues/completed/224-editable-port-names-and-canvas-value-edit.md`\n  — explicitly deferred canvas-value-edit; this is a related but\n  smaller display-only change, not the editing UI from 224\n",

        "text":"Committed (commit `2ce3f72`). Only my 10 files; the other dev's working-tree changes are untouched.\n\nNow the script-location question — a canonical map of every place runnable / loadable code lives in this project:\n\n| Location | What it holds | Who runs it |\n|---|---|---|\n| `scripts/` | Top-level operator scripts: `start-server.sh`, `run-tests.sh`, `create-map.sh`, `open-editor.sh`, `soramech-compile.sh`, `test-server.sh` | You, from a shell |\n| `demo.sh`, `run` (root) | Phase-demo entry points | You, from a shell |\n| `src/` | Editor server + executor + schema/loader in Lua (`001-005-*.lua`), plus phase-3 C runtime (`008-014-*.c`) | The server / pool runtime |\n| `assets/js/` | Editor frontend modules (`001-canvas.js` through `008-source-view.js`) | The browser |\n| `drivers/` | Per-language driver shims (`bash.sh`, `c.sh`, `lua.sh`) that bridge a box invocation to its language | The executor |\n| `langs/<lang>/` | Phase-3 language-spec C glue and per-language build (`spec.c`, `Makefile`, e.g. `langs/bash/bash-server.sh`) | The dispatch layer |\n| `libs/` | Bundled \"library box\" modules every map can `ref` directly: `text.lua`, `files.lua`, `ollama.lua`, `soramech-data.lua`, `dkjson.lua`, plus the C sub-libs `json/` and `task-pool/` | Boxes via `ref` |\n| `maps/<map>/src/` | Per-map user scripts — the actual functions called by each `call` box in that map | The executor when running that map |\n| `tests/maps/<map>/src/` | Same idea but inside the test-map fixtures | The C test binaries |\n| `tests/` | C test binaries and test runners | `scripts/run-tests.sh` |\n\nIf you're looking for something specific and can't find it, the first two places to check are `libs/` (bundled, project-wide) and `maps/<your-map>/src/` (per-map). Everything else is infrastructure.\n\nReady to start on 236 — say go when you've decided."
      }],

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"No, and that's worth flagging — `libs/` is **not** pre-selected by default. Here's what `scripts/create-map.sh` actually does today:\n\nA new map's `meta.json` seeds `src_dirs` with just **the map's own `src/` directory**. The file browser only lists what's in `src_dirs`. So `libs/` won't appear in a freshly-created map until the user adds it via the file-browser's dir-picker (or edits `meta.json` by hand).\n\nThere's a partial-truth-counterpart though: at runtime, the server's `package.path` includes `${DIR}/libs/?.lua`, so a function that does `require(\"text\")` resolves to `libs/text.lua` whether or not the editor knows about it. That means `libs/` is **available for Lua to load**, just **not browseable in the editor by default**.\n\nThat gap is exactly what issue 238 is set up to fix — the config file would carry a `bundled_script_dirs` list (defaulting to `[libs/]`) that `create-map.sh` (or its replacement) drops straight into every new map's `src_dirs`. After 238 lands, \"every new map sees `libs/` in the file browser without the user lifting a finger\" would be the default.\n\nWant me to:\n\n- **(a)** add a small note to 238 making the create-map auto-population explicit (it's implied but not spelled out), or\n- **(b)** open it as a separate tiny issue (\"create-map.sh seeds bundled dirs from server config\") so the two changes can land independently, or\n- **(c)** leave 238 as-is and treat the auto-population as obvious-on-implementation?"
      }],

      "content":"// Source file browser and function signature parser.\n// Renders into the inspector panel: file list → function list → auto-populate box ports.\n\nconst FileBrowser = (() => {\n\n  // {{{ lua_fn_end\n  // Returns the index of the closing 'end'/'until' that matches the function body\n  // starting at body_start. Tracks nesting depth by counting block openers and closers.\n  // Does not attempt to skip string literals — good enough for well-formatted source.\n  function lua_fn_end(content, body_start) {\n    const tok = /\\b(function|if|while|for|repeat|do|end|until)\\b/g;\n    tok.lastIndex = body_start;\n    let depth = 1;\n    let m;\n    while ((m = tok.exec(content)) !== null) {\n      const kw = m[1];\n      if (kw === 'end' || kw === 'until') {\n        depth--;\n        if (depth === 0) return m.index;\n      } else {\n        depth++;\n      }\n    }\n    return content.length;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ parse_lua_returns\n  // Scans a function body for return statements; returns an array of output names.\n  function parse_lua_returns(body) {\n    const re    = /\\breturn\\b\\s*([^\\n]+)/g;\n    const names = new Set();\n    let m;\n    while ((m = re.exec(body)) !== null) {\n      const expr = m[1].replace(/--.*$/, '').trim();\n      if (!expr) continue;\n      // string literals or concat operator mean the whole expression is complex\n      if (/[\"']|\\.\\./.test(expr)) { names.add('result'); continue; }\n      const parts = expr.split(',');\n      parts.forEach(part => {\n        part = part.trim();\n        // bare identifier → use as port name\n        if (/^[a-zA-Z_]\\w*$/.test(part) &&\n            !['nil','true','false','not','and','or','end'].includes(part)) {\n          names.add(part);\n        } else if (parts.length === 1 && part) {\n          // single complex expression → call it \"result\"\n          names.add('result');\n        }\n        // multi-value complex expression with no bare names: skip\n      });\n    }\n    return [...names];\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ parse_lua\n  function parse_lua(content) {\n    const fns    = [];\n    const fn_re  = /^function\\s+M\\.(\\w+)\\s*\\(([^)]*)\\)/mg;\n    let m;\n    while ((m = fn_re.exec(content)) !== null) {\n      const body_start = m.index + m[0].length;\n      const body_end   = lua_fn_end(content, body_start);\n      const body       = content.slice(body_start, body_end);\n      const inputs     = m[2].trim()\n        ? m[2].split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)\n        : [];\n      const outputs    = parse_lua_returns(body);\n      fns.push({ name: m[1], inputs, outputs });\n    }\n    return fns;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ parse_bash_inputs\n  function parse_bash_inputs(body) {\n    const params = {};\n    // local var=\"${N}\" or local var=\"$N\"\n    const local_re = /local\\s+(\\w+)\\s*=\\s*[\"']?\\$\\{?(\\d+)\\}?[\"']?/g;\n    let m;\n    while ((m = local_re.exec(body)) !== null) {\n      params[parseInt(m[2])] = m[1];\n    }\n    if (Object.keys(params).length > 0) {\n      const max = Math.max(...Object.keys(params).map(Number));\n      return Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => params[i + 1] || `arg${i + 1}`);\n    }\n    // fall back: scan for raw $N references\n    const seen = new Set();\n    const pos_re = /\\$\\{?(\\d+)\\}?/g;\n    while ((m = pos_re.exec(body)) !== null) {\n      const n = parseInt(m[1]);\n      if (n > 0) seen.add(n);\n    }\n    if (seen.size > 0) {\n      const max = Math.max(...seen);\n      return Array.from({ length: max }, (_, i) => `arg${i + 1}`);\n    }\n    return [];\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ parse_bash\n  function parse_bash(content) {\n    const fns   = [];\n    const re    = /^(\\w+)\\s*\\(\\s*\\)\\s*\\{/mg;\n    const skip  = new Set(['if','while','for','case','do','done','fi','then','else']);\n    let m;\n    while ((m = re.exec(content)) !== null) {\n      const name = m[1];\n      if (skip.has(name)) continue;\n      const body_start = m.index + m[0].length;\n      const close      = back_btn.textContent = '← ' + filename;\n    back_btn.onclick     = on_back;\n    container.appendChild(back_btn);\n\n    if (fns === null) {\n      const note = document.createElement('div');\n container.appendChild(note);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    fns.forEach(fn => {\n      const row = document.createElement('div');\n      row.className = 'fb-fn-row';\n\n      const name_el = \"use this directory\" confirmation button\n      const sel_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      sel_btn.className   = 'add-port';\n      sel_btn.textContent = '✓ use this directory';\n      sel_btn.style.cssText = 'display:block;width:100%;margin-bottom:8px;' +\n        'color:#4caf7d;border-color:#4caf7d;';\n      sel_btn.onclick = () => on_select(result.path);\n      container.appendChild(sel_btn);\n\n      // parent directory row (except at filesystem root). Prefixed with `·`,\n      // dimmed, no click handler.\n      (result.files || []).forEach(name => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className   = 'fb-file-readonly';\n        row.textContent = '· ' + name;\n        container.appendChild(row);\n      });\n    };\n\n    render_picker();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ show_fb_ctx_menu\n  // Displays a small floating context menu; reuses .ctx-item CSS from the global stylesheet.\n  // items: [{label, action, danger?}]\n  function show_fb_ctx_menu(screen_x, screen_y, items) {\n    let menu = document.getElementById('fb-ctx-menu');\n    if (!menu) {\n      menu = document.createElement('div');\n      menu.id = 'fb-ctx-menu';\n      menu.style.cssText =\n        'position:fixed;background:#181c28;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:4px;padding:4px 0;z-index:1001;min-width:150px;' +\n        'box-shadow:0 4px 16px #00000066;display:none;';\n      document.body.appendChild(menu);\n      // close on any click or Escape — attached once at creation\n      document.addEventListener('click', () => { menu.style.display = 'none'; });\n      document.addEventListener('keydown', e => {\n        if (e.key === 'Escape') menu.style.display = 'none';\n      });\n    }\n    menu.innerHTML = '';\n    items.forEach(item => {\n      const el = document.createElement('div');\n      el.className  = item.danger ? menu.style.display = 'none'; item.action(); });\n      menu.appendChild(el);\n    });\n    menu.style.left    = screen_x + 'px';\n    menu.style.top     = screen_y + 'px';\n    menu.style.display = 'block';\n    const r = menu.getBoundingClientRect();\n    if (r.right  > window.innerWidth)  menu.style.left = (screen_x - r.width)  + 'px';\n    if (r.bottom > window.innerHeight) menu.style.top  = (screen_y - r.height) + 'px';\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ render\n  // Renders the full file browser into container.\n  // on_select(filename, fn_obj) called when the user picks a function.\n  // Groups: [{label, path?, files:[string], fetch_file: async fn(filename)->text}]\n  async function render(container, on_select) {\n    container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note\">loading…</div>';\n\n    // collapsed state: set of group labels\n    const collapsed = new Set();\n\n    // all browseable dirs come from one endpoint — src/ is no longer a special case\n    let src_dirs = [];\n    try {\n      src_dirs = await API.list_extra_src().catch(() => []);\n    } catch (e) {\n      container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note error\">load error: ' + e.message + '</div>';\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // build group list — every entry has a path; DIR .. \"/libs/luasocket/share/lua/5.1/?.lua;\"\n             .. DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\"\n             .. package.path\npackage.cpath = DIR .. \"/libs/luasocket/lib/lua/5.1/?.so;\"\n             .. package.cpath\n\nlocal server_mod = require(\"005-http-server\")\n\n-- {{{ resolve_path\n-- Three path shapes the config can carry (issue 238):\n--   absolute (/x) → returned as-is\n--   home-relative (~/x) → $HOME expansion\n--   project-relative (x) → prefixed with DIR so users can refer to\n--                          in-tree dirs by name without writing the\n--                          absolute mount-point\nlocal function resolve_path(p, project_root)\n    if type(p) ~= \"string\" or p == \"\" then return nil end\n    if p:sub(1, 1) == \"/\" then return p end\n    if p:sub(1, 2) == \"~/\" then\n        local home = os.getenv(\"HOME\") or \"\"\n        return home .. p:sub(2)\n    end\n    return project_root .. \"/\" .. p\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_server_config\n-- Pulls config/editor-server.lua if present; falls back to defaults\n-- when missing, malformed, or partial. The file is OPTIONAL — a user\n-- can run the server with no config at all and get sane behavior.\n-- All paths are resolved here so downstream code sees absolute paths\n-- only.\nlocal function load_server_config(path, project_root)\n    local defaults = {\n        port = 7700,\n        map_root = \"maps\",\n        bundled_script_dirs = { \"libs\" },\n    }\n    local user = {}\n    local ok, loaded = pcall(dofile, path)\n    if ok and type(loaded) == \"table\" then\n        user = loaded\n    end\n    -- Field-by-field merge keeps each missing entry independently\n    -- defaulted, so a config that only sets `port` still benefits\n    -- from the bundled-dirs default.\n    for k, v in pairs(defaults) do\n        if user[k] == nil then user[k] = v end\n    end\n    user.map_root = resolve_path(user.map_root, project_root)\n    local resolved_dirs = {}\n    for _, d in ipairs(user.bundled_script_dirs or {}) do\n        local r = resolve_path(d, project_root)\n        if r then resolved_dirs[#resolved_dirs + 1] = r end\n    end\n    user.bundled_script_dirs = resolved_dirs\n    return user\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main(args)\n    local config = load_server_config(DIR .. \"/config/editor-server.lua\", DIR)\n\n    -- CLI args override config so the existing start-server.sh script\n    -- (which passes positional maps-root + port) keeps working.\n    local maps_root = args[1] or config.map_root\n    local port      = tonumber(args[2]) or config.port\n\n    if not maps_root then\n        io.stderr:write(\"usage: luajit bundled_script_dirs:\")\n    for _, d in ipairs(config.bundled_script_dirs) do\n        print(\"    - \" .. d)\n    end\n\n    server_mod.serve({\n        maps_root    = maps_root,\n        port     "newString":"        const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n        lbl.className   = 'fb-header';\n        lbl.textContent = group.label;\n        hdr.appendChild(lbl);\n\n        // Bundled dirs (issue 238) get a small tag so the user can\n        // tell their own toolbox apart from the editor-wide defaults.\n        if (group.kind === 'bundled') {\n          const tag = document.createElement('span');\n          tag.textContent = ' bundled';\n          tag.style.cssText = 'font-size:9px;color:#4caf7d;margin-left:6px;' +\n            'border:1px solid #4caf7d;padding:0 4px;border-radius:2px;';\n          hdr.appendChild(tag);\n        }\n\n        hdr.onclick = () => {\n          if (collapsed.has(collapse_key)) collapsed.delete(collapse_key);\n          else collapsed.add(collapse_key);\n          show_file_list();\n        };\n\n        // Right-click on a map-owned dir header offers \"hide\n        // directory\" — removes it from meta.json. Bundled dirs skip\n        // this menu entirely: they aren't in meta.json (they come\n        // from the server's config file), so removing them from\n        // meta.json would be a no-op the user would then have to\n        // figure out. The honest answer is \"edit the config file.\"\n        if (group.kind !== 'bundled') {\n          hdr.addEventListener('contextmenu', e => {\n            e.preventDefault();\n            show_fb_ctx_menu(e.clientX, e.clientY, [{\n              label:  'hide directory',\n              danger: true,\n              action: async () => {\n                try {\n                  const meta = await API.get_meta();\n                  // Same migration rationale as add: use groups as source\n                  // of truth. Only map-owned paths get written back —\n                  // bundled paths are filtered out so a stale bundled\n                  // entry never bleeds into meta.json.\n                  const dirs = groups\n                    .filter(g => g.kind !== 'bundled' && g.path !== group.path)\n                    .map(g => g.path);\n                  await API.put_meta({ ...meta, src_dirs: dirs });\n                  render(container, on_select);\n                } catch (err) {\n                  show_file_list();\n                  const note = document.createElement('div');\n                  note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n                  note.textContent = 'could not hide dir: ' + err.message;\n                  container.insertBefore(note, container.firstChild);\n                }\n              },\n            }]);\n          });\n        }",
    "structuredPatch":[{

      "content":"end\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend",

          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"-- {{{ file_exists\nlocal function file_exists(path)\n    local f = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then return false end\n    f:close()\n    return true\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ generate_default_config\n-- Writes DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT to `path`, creating the parent dir if\n-- needed. Called from load_server_config when the file is missing\n-- so first-time users start from an editable template rather than\n-- a \"where do I customize this?\" mystery. The message prints to\n-- stdout so the action is visible in the boot log.\nlocal function generate_default_config(path)\n    print(\"generating config file at \" .. path .. \" ...\")\n    local parent = path:match(\"^(.*)/[^/]+$\")\n    if parent then os.execute(\"mkdir -p '\" .. parent .. \"'\") end\n    local f, err = io.open(path, \"w\")\n    if not f then\n        io.stderr:write(\"could not write config file: \" .. tostring(err) .. \"\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n    f:write(DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT)\n    f:close()\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_server_config\n-- Two paths through this function (issue 238):\n--   1. Config file present → dofile it; any missing field falls back\n--      to the value embedded in DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT (parsed once at\n--      startup) so partial configs keep working.\n--   2. Config file absent → generate the default template at the\n--      target path, then load the freshly-written file. The\n--      hard-wired defaults are NOT a separate code path — they live\n--      in DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT and are read back from disk after\n--      generation, so the on-disk file is always the source of\n--      truth on the next boot.\n-- All paths are resolved here so downstream code sees absolute\n-- paths only.\nlocal function load_server_config(path, project_root)\n    if not file_exists(path) then\n        generate_default_config(path)\n    end\n\n    local ok, user = pcall(dofile, path)\n    if not ok or type(user) ~= \"table\" then\n        io.stderr:write(\"config file at \" .. path .. \" did not return a table: \"\n            .. tostring(user) .. \"\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    -- Parse the embedded template separately so we can use it for\n    -- field-level fallbacks. dostring via load() — runs in-memory,\n    -- no second disk read.\n    local defaults_fn = load(DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT, \"default-config\", \"t\")\n    local defaults    = defaults_fn and defaults_fn() or {}\n    for k, v in pairs(defaults) do\n        if user[k] == nil then user[k] = v end\n    end\n\n    user.map_root = resolve_path(user.map_root, project_root)\n    local resolved_dirs = {}\n    for _, d in ipairs(user.bundled_script_dirs or {}) do\n        local r = resolve_path(d, project_root)\n        if r then resolved_dirs[#resolved_dirs + 1] = r end\n    end\n    user.bundled_script_dirs = resolved_dirs\n    return user\nend\n-- }}}",

The message prints to\n-- stdout so the action is visible in the boot log.\nlocal function generate_default_config(path)\n    print(\"generating config file at \" .. path .. \" ...\")\n    local parent = path:match(\"^(.*)/[^/]+$\")\n    if parent then os.execute(\"mkdir -p '\" .. parent .. \"'\") end\n    local f, err = io.open(path, \"w\")\n    if not f then\n        io.stderr:write(\"could not write config file: \" .. tostring(err) .. \"\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n    f:write(DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT)\n    f:close()\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_server_config\n-- Two paths through this function (issue 238):\n--   1. Config file present → dofile it; any missing field falls back\n--      to the value embedded in DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT (parsed once at\n--      startup) so partial configs keep working.\n--   2. Config file absent → generate the default template at the\n--      target path, then load the freshly-written file. The\n--      hard-wired defaults are NOT a separate code path — they live\n--      in DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT and are read back from disk after\n--      generation, so the on-disk file is always the source of\n--      truth on the next boot.\n-- All paths are resolved here so downstream code sees absolute\n-- paths only.\nlocal function load_server_config(path, project_root)\n    if not file_exists(path) then\n        generate_default_config(path)\n    end\n\n    local ok, user = pcall(dofile, path)\n    if not ok or type(user) ~= \"table\" then\n        io.stderr:write(\"config file at \" .. path .. \" did not return a table: \"\n            .. tostring(user) .. \"\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    -- Parse the embedded template separately so we can use it for\n    -- field-level fallbacks. dostring via load() — runs in-memory,\n    -- no second disk read.\n    local defaults_fn = load(DEFAULT_CONFIG_TEXT, \"default-config\", \"t\")\n    local defaults    = defaults_fn and defaults_fn() or {}\n    for k, v in pairs(defaults) do\n        if user[k] == nil then user[k] = v end\n    end\n\n    user.map_root = resolve_path(user.map_root, project_root)\n    local resolved_dirs = {}\n    for _, d in ipairs(user.bundled_script_dirs or {}) do\n        local r = resolve_path(d, project_root)\n        if r then resolved_dirs[#resolved_dirs + 1] = r end\n    end\n    user.bundled_script_dirs = resolved_dirs\n    return user\nend\n-- }}}",

The server\n-- prints the resolved settings on boot so you can confirm what's in\n-- effect.\n--\n-- Path resolution\n--   /abs/path  → used as-is\n--   ~/under-home → $HOME expansion\n--   relative   → resolved against the project root (the `DIR` constant\n--                in src/006-server-main.lua)\n\nreturn {\n  -- TCP port the HTTP server binds to.\n  port = 7700,\n\n  -- Directory holding map subdirectories. The editor lists subdirs\n  -- of this path in its map picker.\n  map_root = \"maps\",\n\n  -- Bundled script directories — every map sees these in the file\n  -- browser without per-map setup. They're merged in alongside the\n  -- map's own meta.json src_dirs at runtime, not seeded into each\n  -- new map's meta.json. Add your personal library directory here\n  -- (absolute path or ~ shorthand) to make it available everywhere.\n  -- A map can hide one of these for itself by adding its path to\n  -- the meta.json `hidden_bundled_dirs` list (the editor writes\n  -- this when you right-click \"hide directory\" on a bundled entry).\n  bundled_script_dirs = {\n    \"libs\",\n  },\n}\n]]\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ resolve_path\n-- Three path shapes the config can carry (issue 238):\n--   absolute (/x) → returned as-is\n--   home-relative (~/x) → $HOME expansion\n--   project-relative (x) → prefixed with DIR so users can refer to\n--                          in-tree dirs by name without writing the\n--                          absolute mount-point\nlocal function resolve_path(p, project_root)\n    if type(p) ~= \"string\" or p == \"\" then return nil end\n    if p:sub(1, 1) == \"/\" then return p end\n    if p:sub(1, 2) == \"~/\" then\n        local home = os.getenv(\"HOME\") or \"\"\n        return home .. p:sub(2)\n    end\n    return project_root .. \"/\" .. p\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ load_server_config\n-- Pulls config/editor-server.lua if present; falls back to defaults\n-- when missing, malformed, or partial. The file is OPTIONAL — a user\n-- can run the server with no config at all and get sane behavior.\n-- All paths are resolved here so downstream code sees absolute paths\n-- only.\nlocal function a config that only sets `port` still benefits\n    -- from the bundled-dirs default.\n    for k, v in pairs(defaults) do\n        if user[k] == nil then user[k] = v end\n    end\n    user.map_root = resolve_path(user.map_root, project_root)\n    local resolved_dirs = {}\n    for _, d in ipairs(user.bundled_script_dirs or {}) do\n        local r = resolve_path(d, project_root)\n        if r then resolved_dirs[#resolved_dirs + 1] = r end\n    end\n    user.bundled_script_dirs = resolved_dirs\n    return user\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main(args)\n    local config = handle:read(\"*l\")\n    handle:close()\n\n    print(\"soramech-server config:\")\n    print(\"  port:                \" .. port)\n    print(\"  map_root:            \" .. maps_root)\n    print(\"  bundled_script_dirs:\")\n    for _, d in ipairs(config.bundled_script_dirs) do\n        print(\"    - \" .. d)\n    end\n\n    server_mod.serve({\n        maps_root    = maps_root,\n        port         = port,\n        bundled_dirs = config.bundled_script_dirs,\n    })\nend\n-- }}}\n\nmain(arg)\n",

    "newString":"        // Every dir gets a \"bundled\" tag — they're all library\n        // directories from the map's point of view, whether the\n        // path lives in the editor config or in this map's meta.\n        // The user asked for a uniform treatment (issue 238) so the\n        // visual cue doesn't single one kind out as special.\n        const tag = document.createElement('span');\n        tag.textContent = ' bundled';\n        tag.style.cssText = 'font-size:9px;color:#4caf7d;margin-left:6px;' +\n          'border:1px solid #4caf7d;padding:0 4px;border-radius:2px;';\n        hdr.appendChild(tag);\n\n        hdr.onclick = () => {\n          if (collapsed.has(collapse_key)) collapsed.delete(collapse_key);\n          else collapsed.add(collapse_key);\n          show_file_list();\n        };\n\n        // Right-click → \"hide directory\" works on every group. The\n        // storage differs by kind: map dirs come out of src_dirs;\n        // editor-wide bundled dirs are recorded in\n        // hidden_bundled_dirs (an opt-out list the server checks\n        // when merging in the config defaults). The user\n        // experiences both as the same action.\n        hdr.addEventListener('contextmenu', e => {\n          e.preventDefault();\n          show_fb_ctx_menu(e.clientX, e.clientY, [{\n            label:  'hide directory',\n            danger: true,\n            action: async () => {\n              try {\n                const meta = await API.get_meta();\n                let patch;\n                if (group.kind === 'bundled') {\n                  // record the opt-out; the server filters this\n                  // path out of the bundled list on next load\n                  const hidden = Array.isArray(meta.hidden_bundled_dirs)\n                    ? meta.hidden_bundled_dirs.slice() : [];\n                  if (!hidden.includes(group.path)) hidden.push(group.path);\n                  patch = { ...meta, hidden_bundled_dirs: hidden };\n                } else {\n                  // drop from src_dirs; bundled paths never bleed\n                  // into the per-map list\n                  const dirs = groups\n                    .filter(g => g.kind !== 'bundled' && g.path !== group.path)\n                    .map(g => g.path);\n                  patch = { ...meta, src_dirs: dirs };\n                }\n                await API.put_meta(patch);\n                render(container, on_select);\n              } catch (err) {\n                show_file_list();\n                const note = document.createElement('div');\n                note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n                note.textContent = 'could not hide dir: ' + err.message;\n                container.insertBefore(note, container.firstChild);\n              }\n            },\n          }]);\n        });",

The honest answer is \"edit the config file.\"\n        if (group.kind !== 'bundled') {\n          hdr.addEventListener('contextmenu', e => {\n            e.preventDefault();\n            show_fb_ctx_menu(e.clientX, e.clientY, [{\n              label:  'hide directory',\n              danger: true,\n              action: async () => {\n                try {\n                  const meta = await API.get_meta();\n                  // Same migration rationale as add: use groups as source\n                  // of truth. Only map-owned paths get written back —\n                  // bundled paths are filtered out so a stale bundled\n                  // entry never bleeds into meta.json.\n                  const dirs = groups\n                    .filter(g => g.kind !== 'bundled' && g.path !== group.path)\n                    .map(g => g.path);\n                  await API.put_meta({ ...meta, src_dirs: dirs });\n                  render(container, on_select);\n                } catch (err) {\n                  show_file_list();\n                  const note = document.createElement('div');\n                  note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n                  note.textContent = 'could not hide dir: ' + err.message;\n                  container.insertBefore(note, container.firstChild);\n                }\n              },\n            }]);\n          });\n        }",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"        // Every dir gets a \"bundled\" tag — they're all library\n        // directories from the map's point of view, whether the\n        // path lives in the editor config or in this map's meta.\n        // The user asked for a uniform treatment (issue 238) so the\n        // visual cue doesn't single one kind out as special.\n        const tag = document.createElement('span');\n        tag.textContent = ' bundled';\n        tag.style.cssText = 'font-size:9px;color:#4caf7d;margin-left:6px;' +\n          'border:1px solid #4caf7d;padding:0 4px;border-radius:2px;';\n        hdr.appendChild(tag);\n\n        hdr.onclick = () => {\n          if (collapsed.has(collapse_key)) collapsed.delete(collapse_key);\n          else collapsed.add(collapse_key);\n          show_file_list();\n        };\n\n        // Right-click → \"hide directory\" works on every group. The\n        // storage differs by kind: map dirs come out of src_dirs;\n        // editor-wide bundled dirs are recorded in\n        // hidden_bundled_dirs (an opt-out list the server checks\n        // when merging in the config defaults).           "old_string":"-- {{{ resolve_src_dirs\n-- Returns the unified browseable-dir list for a map: every entry is\n-- {path, kind} where kind = \"map\" for map-owned dirs (the map's own\n-- src/ and any user-added extras stored in meta.json) or \"bundled\"\n-- for config-driven shared dirs that every map sees (issue 238).\n-- Map dirs come first so the user's own work sits at the top of the\n-- file browser; bundled dirs follow as a stable default suffix.\n-- Migration: if meta.json has no src_dirs, synthesizes from implicit\n-- src/ + the older extra_src_dirs field.\nlocal function resolve_src_dirs(meta, maps_root, map_name)\n    local out = {}\n    if meta.src_dirs then\n        for _, d in ipairs(meta.src_dirs) do\n            out[#out + 1] = { path = d, kind = \"map\" }\n        end\n    else\n        out[#out + 1] = { path = maps_root .. \"/\" .. map_name .. \"/src\", kind = \"map\" }\n        for _, d in ipairs(meta.extra_src_dirs or {}) do\n            out[#out + 1] = { path = d, kind = \"map\" }\n        end\n    end\n    -- Per-map opt-out for bundled dirs: a map can list paths in\n    -- meta.hidden_bundled_dirs to skip them. Same hide gesture the\n    -- user does for map-owned dirs, surfaced through the editor's\n    -- right-click menu so the two kinds feel identical to use.\n    local hidden = {}\n    for _, p in ipairs(meta.hidden_bundled_dirs or {}) do hidden[p] = true end\n    for _, d in ipairs(bundled_dirs) do\n        if not hidden[d] then\n            out[#out + 1] = { path = d, kind = \"bundled\" }\n        end\n    end\n    return out\nend\n-- }}}",
          "replace_all":false,
          "new_string":"-- {{{ resolve_src_dirs\n-- Returns the unified browseable-dir list for a map. Every entry is\n-- {path, kind} with one of three kinds (issue 238):\n--   default — the map's own src/ directory, always present\n--   added   — a dir the user attached to this map via \"+ library dir\"\n--   bundled — an editor-wide default from config/editor-server.lua\n-- The split between default and added isn't about how they behave at\n-- runtime (both live in meta.src_dirs) — it's so the file browser\n-- can mark \"ships with the map\" entries differently from \"user\n-- opted in\" entries.     "originalFile":"# 238 — Editor HTTP server config file (default bundled-script locations)\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe editor's HTTP server (`src/005-http-server.lua`, issue 105) is\nlaunched with map-relative paths discovered at startup time. The\nfile browser (issue 211, 211a) sees the map's own `src/` directory\nplus the unified pipeline dirs the runner sets up, but the set of\n\"bundled / default\" library locations the editor offers is\nhard-coded in the server / file-browser logic.\n\nIf a user wants to drop in their own personal library of bundled\nscripts (e.g. their own `text-extras.lua`, their own\n`my-team-helpers/` directory) and have the editor's file browser\ntreat them as first-class default refs, there is no per-deployment\nway to point the server at additional directories. They would have\nto edit the server source.\n\nThere is also no record of the editor's runtime configuration —\nports, default map dir, asset dir, the bundled lib dirs — in a\nconfig file the user can read or version. The defaults live in\ncode.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nIntroduce a config file the editor's HTTP server reads at startup\nto learn:\n\n- **Server port** (default `7474` or whichever current default).\n- **Map root directory** (default `maps/`).\n- **Bundled script locations** — a list of directory paths the\n  file browser exposes as default-available refs, distinct from\n  the current map's own `src/`. Default list includes `libs/`.\n- **Asset directory** for the editor (default `assets/`).\n- **Log / tmp directory** if relevant (per the project's tmp\n  symlink convention).\n\nEach entry has a sensible default; missing entries fall back to\nthose defaults. The user can override any subset by editing the\nfile.\n\n### File location and format\n\nPath: `config/editor-server.lua` (returns a Lua table) or\n`config/editor-server.json`. Lean toward the Lua table — every\nother config in this project is Lua, and a Lua return-table lets\nthe user compute paths if needed (e.g. `os.getenv(\"HOME\") .. \"/my-libs\"`).\n\nShape:\n\n```lua\nreturn {\n  port = 7474,\n  map_root = \"maps\",\n  asset_dir = \"assets\",\n  bundled_script_dirs = {\n    \"libs\",           -- the in-tree default\n    -- \"~/.soramech/my-libs\",  -- example user override\n  },\n  tmp_dir = \"tmp\",\n}\n```\n\nA startup helper in `src/006-server-main.lua` loads the config,\nfills in defaults, and passes the resolved table down to the HTTP\nserver module. The server prints the resolved config on boot so\nthe user can confirm what's in effect.\n\n### File browser surfacing\n\nThe file browser (issue 211 + 211a) currently lists the map's own\n`src/` and the pipeline-resolved bundled dirs. With this config in\nplace, the bundled list comes from `bundled_script_dirs` directly.\nA second pane (or expandable section per dir) labels each entry by\nits source directory so the user can tell their own bundle apart\nfrom the in-tree `libs/`.\n\n### Why a file, not CLI flags\n\nTwo reasons:\n1. Reproducibility — the config file checks into a personal dotfile\n   or repo, and the editor starts up the same way every time.\n2. Discoverability — a user reading their `config/` directory sees\n   what's customizable. CLI flags are invisible until the user runs\n   `--help`.\n\nCLI flags can layer on top if needed (a `--config-file` override),\nbut the file is the primary mechanism.\n\n### Defaults vs explicit\n\nThe server still works with no config file present — every field\nhas a default and the file is optional. Creating the file is a\n\"customize me\" gesture, not a setup requirement.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Per-map config overrides**: a map could ship its own\n  `config/editor-server.lua` that adds its own bundled dirs. Useful?\n  Probably yes long-term, but defer until a real use case appears.\n  The global config is enough for now.\n- **Path resolution**: bundled dirs as absolute paths, project-\n  relative, or both? Both. If the path starts with `/` or `~`,\n  treat as absolute (after `~` expansion); otherwise resolve\n  against the project root. Document this in a comment at the top\n  of the config file.\n- **Hot reload**: changes to the config file requiring a server\n  restart vs picked up on next request? Restart is simpler and\n  matches the existing model. Hot reload is a separate issue if\n  ever wanted.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. New file `config/editor-server.lua` (or a documented sample\n   under `config/editor-server.example.lua`) with the schema above\n   and the defaults filled in.\n2. `src/006-server-main.lua` — `load_server_config(path)`:\n   - `pcall(dofile, path)` — fall back to empty table if missing.\n   - Merge over a defaults table.\n   - `~` expansion on string paths.\n   - Print resolved config on stdout at boot.\n3. `src/005-http-server.lua` — accept the resolved config table as\n   its constructor argument. Use `bundled_script_dirs` in the\n   `handle_list_src` family so the file browser sees them.\n4. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — render bundled dirs as a\n   labeled second pane, separate from the current map's `src/`.\n5. Document the file in `docs/`: a new short section in\n   `docs/005-language-specs.md` (or its own page) describing the\n   config schema and the path resolution rules.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — server module to parameterize\n- `src/006-server-main.lua` — boot point that loads config\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — UI surface for bundled dirs\n- `issues/completed/105-http-server-file-crud.md` — original server\n- `issues/completed/211-file-browser-library-dirs.md` — current\n  library-dir discovery this issue parameterizes\n- `issues/completed/211a-unify-src-dirs-pipeline.md` — pipeline\n  unification that influences how bundled paths get resolved\n- `issues/237-string-manipulation-library-expansion.md` — paired\n  issue; this config file makes \"what counts as bundled\" pluggable\n- `docs/000-table-of-contents.md` — new doc page to add when the\n  config schema doc is written\n",

          "command":"git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nBundled-script directories every map sees by default (issue 238)\n\nThe editor now reads a config file on boot — first run generates it\nfrom a template, later runs respect whatever the user has edited.\nIts bundled-scripts list flows into every map's file browser\nalongside the map's own src/ and any per-map additions, so the\nstandard toolbox shows up without the user touching meta.json.\n\nIn the browser, each directory wears one of three labels under the\nhood: the map's own folder, a folder the user attached themselves,\nand an editor-wide default. The first and third advertise\nthemselves with a small \"bundled\" tag — the things that arrived for\nfree. The middle stays plain so the user can see at a glance what\nthey opted into. Right-click → hide works the same on all three;\nthe only difference is where the opt-out is recorded (per-map for\nthe first two, a meta-side hidden-list for the third).\n\nGeneration prints \"generating config file at …\" the first time it\nfires, so the boot log is honest about the side-effect. A malformed\nconfig errors out clearly instead of silently overwriting the\nuser's file. Partial configs (missing fields) fall back field-by-\nfield against the same template that seeded the file, so editing\nout one knob doesn't break the others.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

        "content":"==================== 230\n# 230 — Required inputs, the optional flag, and no-null-from-missing\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nA box's input port can be left without a wire and without a literal\nvalue. The phase 2 executor runs the box anyway; the function on\nthe other end gets `nil` (Lua), unset (Bash), or whatever default\nthe language hands a missing positional arg.         "text":"Here's the unstarted set, grouped by area:\n\n**Editor / phase-2 extensions** — fully unstarted, ready for pickup:\n\n| ID | Title | One-line summary |\n|---|---|---|\n| **229** | `read` / `write` box kinds (language-agnostic IO) | Three box kinds — `call` (existing), `read` (path→contents), `write` (path+value→done). Optional outputs are discarded when no wire. Bigger scope: touches schema, loader, dispatch (phase-3 territory). |\n| **230** | Required inputs and the optional flag | Every input must have a wire, a literal, or `optional: true` at compile time. Catches silent-nil bugs where a missing wire produces unset args at runtime. |\n| **231** | Move signature parsers into `langs/<name>/parser.js` | Extract `parse_lua` / `parse_bash` out of the file browser into per-language ES modules, so adding a new language doesn't require editing the editor. |\n| **233** | Unified routing schema for branching boxes | Every call box carries an explicit `routing` field (plain / comparator / iterator / etc.) instead of inferring the kind from sibling fields. Replaces the current ad-hoc comparator+iterator schemas. |\n| **234** | Middle-click duplicates the selected box | Short middle-mouse click on the canvas while a box is selected creates a duplicate with the same ref/fn, literal values, and incoming wires. |\n| **236** | Box header = filename, output label = `fn()` | Box header shows the basename of `ref`; output port shows `fn_name()` for `call` boxes. Per-kind defaults for non-call boxes. User label still overrides. |\n| **237** | String-manipulation library expansion | Grow `libs/text.lua` with upper/lower/trim/replace/replace_first/contains/starts_with/ends_with/length/substring. |\n\n**Phase-3 runtime** — the other dev's territory; mostly already in flight:\n\n- **301–312, 314** all marked \"in progress\" — pool, slot store, language specs, dispatch, graph loader, build system, etc.\n- **313** is research/blocked (whole-program same-language merge)\n- **315** — Reference-counted compiled-map artifacts (don't clobber a build that other tools are using)\n- **316** — Simple test runner script (run existing test binaries without rebuilding everything)\n- **317** — Language spec JSON bridge for data boxes (per-language to-JSON / from-JSON callbacks, so a Lua data box can author with native tables)\n\nIf you want to keep working in the editor, **234** is the smallest visible win, **236** is the most stylistically impactful (every box's header changes), and **237** is pure additive scripting with no UI risk. **229** is biggest because it crosses into the phase-3 runtime — best deferred until the dispatch layer settles."

          "new_string":"  // {{{ default_header\n  // The box header text used when `box.label` is unset (issue 236).\n  // Three cases:\n  //   call    — basename of `ref`, the source file the box calls\n  //   other   — the kind name, plain\n  //   unknown — fall back to the box id so nothing renders blank\n  // Exported so the inspector can show it as the label-field\n  // placeholder, keeping the inspector and canvas in sync about\n  // \"what would render if I left this empty\".\n  function default_header(box) {\n    if (box.kind === 'call' && box.ref) {\n      const parts = String(box.ref).split('/');\n      return parts[parts.length - 1] || box.ref;\n    }\n    return KIND_HEADER[box.kind] || box.kind || box.id;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ output_label_text\n  // Picks the string drawn to the LEFT of an output port dot\n  // (issue 236). Two paths:\n  //   p.name set → render it (comparator branches, iterator slots)\n  //   p.name null, box is a call → render `fn()` so the wire reads\n  //     as \"the return value of calling fn\"\n  //   otherwise → null, draw no label\n  function output_label_text(box, p) {\n    if (p.name) return p.name;\n    if (box.kind === 'call' && box.fn) return box.fn + '()';\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_has_incoming_wire",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/002-boxes.js"

console.log(`FAIL ${i}: hdr got=${got} expect=${c.hdr_label}`); }\n    else console.log(`OK ${i}: label override → ${got}`);\n  } else {\n    const got = default_header(c.box);\n    if (got !== c.hdr) { fail++; console.log(`FAIL ${i}: hdr got=${got} expect=${c.hdr}`); }\n    else console.log(`OK ${i}: hdr=${got}`);\n  }\n  if (c.out !== undefined) {\n    const got = output_label_text(c.box, {name:null});\n    if (got !== c.out) { fail++; console.log(`FAIL ${i}: out got=${got} expect=${c.out}`); }\n    else console.log(`  out=${got}`);\n  }\n});\n\n// branch-name output preserved\nconst branch = output_label_text({kind:'comparator'}, {name:'lt'});\nconsole.log(branch === 'lt' ? 'OK branch label preserved' : 'FAIL branch label: ' + branch);\n\nconsole.log(fail === 0 ? '\\nALL PASS' : `\\n${fail} FAIL`);\nprocess.exit(fail);\nEOF\nnode /tmp/test-236.js",
          "description":"Unit test the new pure functions"
        }

For `call` boxes it's the\n  basename of `ref`; for the other kinds it's a small lookup\n  table (`branch`, `data`, `comparator`, `iterator` — full kind\n  names, no abbreviations). Exported so the inspector can show\n  it as the label-input placeholder, keeping inspector and\n  canvas in sync about \"what shows when this field is blank.\"\n- `output_label_text(box, p)` — the string to the LEFT of an\n  output port dot. Named ports (comparator branches, iterator\n  slots) keep their existing names; a `call` box's single\n  null-named output now renders as `fn_name()`. Anything else\n  renders nothing, same as before.\n\n`draw_box` routes its header through `box.label || default_header(box)`\nand its output-label loop through `output_label_text`. The\nsingle-output `fn()` label uses the kind color (the existing\ndot color), matching how comparator branches paint themselves.\n\n`assets/js/004-inspector.js` sets the title input's\n`placeholder` to `Boxes.default_header(box)`. The label-input\nwrite path is unchanged — typing into the field updates\n`current_box.label`, which on the next render-pass wins over\nthe default.\n\nTwo call sites where the file browser writes `ref`/`fn` onto\nthe current box now also rewrite `box.label` to the new\nfilename — but ONLY when the new file differs from the\nprevious one. Picking a different function from the same file\nleaves the label alone, so user-customized labels survive\nfunction swaps within a module. Different file → label snaps\nto the new basename, matching the canvas-header convention.\n\nTested with the 10-case node script (call w/ ref+fn, label\noverride, every non-call kind, unknown kind, missing kind →\nid fallback, branch name preserved as output label).
